newsitem.title: TURKEY: Tofas workers on 6-day compulsory leave.
newsitem.headline: Tofas workers on 6-day compulsory leave.

text.p: Turkey's leading car maker Tofas Turk Otomobil Fabrikasi put all of its 4,500 workers on compulsory leave from Wednesday until next Tuesday after capacity usage fell below 40 percent at its Bursa plant.
In a statement sent to the Istanbul stock exchange, Tofas said the low capacity usage necessitated an immediate switch to single-shift production from two.
"Workers will receive 76 percent of their normal pay during the (six-day) compulsory leave and single-shift production will begin on November 26 (Tuesday)," the statement said.

Tofas had announced last week its plans to cut production from two shifts to one from December 2 by putting 1,011 workers, or 22 percent of its workforce, on compulsory leave with 76 percent pay and to make them redundant from January 2, 1997.

The company's layoff plans were due to a sharp fall in demand amid expectations of cheaper car imports after two recent cabinet decrees which conditionally allowed a limited number of duty-free passenger car imports from June 1, 1997.

Turkish residents and expatriates will be allowed to bring in one foreign car of up to five years of age without import tax if they deposit 50,000 marks for a year at public Ziraat Bank by end-1996. They will also earn a 10 percent annual interest.
The scheme is part of the government's two packages revealed since late July to boost state revenues.
